result_semantic_payload.summary: The USDT transfers visible in this device's logs are all attributed to the account string 'chenwei', recorded in /logs/app1.log: 30000 USDT on 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT on 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both destined for TBait8888Wallet (total 42000 USDT). Both transfers sit inside a chenwei login session (logins 09:14:22 from 203.0.113.77 and 22:41:10 from 198.51.100.23; the first session ends with a LOGOUT at 09:16:44). A third account, liuyu, appears in app1.log but only performs a DOWNLOAD of /reports/q1-analysis.pdf and no transfer. The second system's log, /logs/app2.log, contains the same account string 'chenwei' on 2024-02-20/21/22 performing UPLOAD, LOGIN and PRINT actions from private RFC1918 addresses 10.20.0.5 and 10.20.0.9, with no USDT activity at all. On the identity question: the README.txt case note explicitly states the two systems are 'unrelated internal systems' that 'share no account database', so the matching 'chenwei' string across the two logs is NOT provable to be one person — it is a name collision candidate only. Nothing in the evidence links the two systems' chenwei accounts (no shared account database, no shared authenticator, no correlated IPs, no common device identifier, no certificate, no session token). What the evidence does support is a single account STRING on each system, and a plausible but unproven link between them (same spelling, same person's likely real name per the README's employee roster, chenwei = finance dept). Attribution of the transfers to the human 'chenwei' is likewise only as strong as the log's own account field plus session adjacency — the logs carry no password hash, no MFA record, no biometric, no machine identifier, so account compromise of the chenwei account on system 1 cannot be excluded. Additionally, this task exposes NO Windows-derived evidence whatsoever: get_task_context reports platforms=[] and source_scopes=[], and the only three files are two plain-text application logs and one README. No registry, Event Log, Prefetch, Amcache, SRUM, ShimCache, shell history, USB or file-system timeline data exists, so the Windows specialist profile's core corroboration rules (execution claims require prefetch/amcache corroboration; logon events correlated with account and source-IP context) cannot be applied. All findings below are therefore limited to the two text logs and the case note.

claim_candidates.text: Two USDT transfers appear in /logs/app1.log, both attributed to the account string 'chenwei': 30000 USDT to TBait8888Wallet at 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT to TBait8888Wallet at 2024-03-02 22:43:55, totalling 42000 USDT.

The first transfer occurred 41 seconds after a successful chenwei login from 203.0.113.77 at 09:14:22 and before the corresponding LOGOUT at 09:16:44; the second transfer occurred 165 seconds after a successful chenwei login from 198.51.100.23 at 22:41:10. Both transfers are therefore temporally nested inside chenwei sessions in that log.

The account string 'liuyu' appears in /logs/app1.log (login 2024-03-05 11:02:31 from 203.0.113.77, DOWNLOAD of /reports/q1-analysis.pdf at 11:04:19) and is associated with no USDT transfer in the available evidence.

The account string 'chenwei' also appears in /logs/app2.log on 2024-02-20 through 2024-02-22, performing UPLOAD of /shared/annual-plan.docx, LOGIN from 10.20.0.5 and 10.20.0.9, and PRINT to HQ-3F; that log contains no USDT or transfer events of any kind.

The case note README.txt states the two systems are unrelated internal systems that share no account database. Consequently the identical 'chenwei' account string on the two systems cannot be treated as evidence that the same person performed the actions on both; the evidence supports at most a name collision between two independent account namespaces.
limitations: README.txt is a case note, not an authenticated artifact of either system; its statement about shared account databases is unverified against the systems themselves.

claim_candidates.text: No artifact in this task links the chenwei account on system 1 to the chenwei account on system 2: no shared account database, no shared IP (203.0.113.77 / 198.51.100.23 vs 10.20.0.5 / 10.20.0.9), no machine identifier, no session token, no certificate, no timestamp overlap (Feb 20-22 vs Mar 1-5). The two systems are separated by roughly 7-10 days with no bridging event.

The evidence does not support concluding that a human named chenwei personally executed the transfers. limitations: Absence of authentication artifacts is a limitation of the captured data, not proof of compromise.
